Creative.manifesto: Most industrial robots are designed for engineering integration teams and operated remotely. We started The Assembly Floor Co because the actual best industrial robotics works with the human operators on the floor — visible status, audible cues, reconfiguration tools that anyone on the team can use. The robots are floor team members, not floor replacements.
Creative.industrySummary: Collaborative robotics (cobots) has matured into a recognized category but most cobot brands focus on safety certification rather than on operator collaboration as a creative design philosophy. There is real space for a creative-led brand that explicitly positions on robot-as-floor-team-member.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Universal Robots (universal-robots.com) plays the collaborative-robotics reference at scale. Rethink Robotics (formerly rethinkrobotics.com) was the closest spiritual peer. Doosan Robotics (doosanrobotics.com) holds the modern cobot peer slot. Franka Emika (franka.de) sits in the considered-modern collaborative peer position. We sit alongside Universal Robots with a stronger operator-collaboration creative position.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Assembly Floor Co is a creative-led industrial robotics brand designing collaborative robots for assembly floors with hardware deliberately reconfigurable by floor-team operators.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the operator-collaboration premise. Visible status. Audible cues. Reconfiguration by the floor team rather than by remote engineering.

targetAudience.primary: Operations directors, manufacturing engineers, and floor-team leads at small to mid-sized manufacturers integrating collaborative robots into human-operated assembly lines.
behaviors: Run small to mid-sized assembly operations with human operators.
Care about operator-friendliness of factory equipment.
Train floor team members to operate and reconfigure equipment.
Renew on multi-year service contracts.
motivations: Want robots designed to work with floor operators.
Want reconfiguration tools that floor teams can use.
Want visible-status hardware rather than remote-only dashboards.

dos: Publish the quarterly essay on human-robot collaboration.
Photograph robots on actual assembly floors, with operators visible.
Reference operator training programmes by name.

messagingPillars.name: Visible status hardware
messagingPillars.description: Every robot ships with visible status lights, audible cues, and mechanical position indicators. The floor team can read the robot's state without a dashboard.

messagingPillars.name: Operator reconfiguration
messagingPillars.description: Reconfiguration tooling is designed for use by floor-team operators, not just integration engineers. Training programmes accompany every installation.

messagingPillars.name: Quarterly essay
messagingPillars.description: The brand publishes a long-form essay on human-robot collaboration every quarter — case studies, operator interviews, design philosophy.

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark — The Assembly Floor Co set in a quiet display serif with a small illustration of a robotic arm beside it. The mark feels printed on a factory-floor signage panel.
